task_prompt:
You are the continuity editor for episode 2 of "The Dead Drop".
SERIES: The Dead Drop | A gig-economy delivery rider discovers his route consists entirely of addresses belonging to people who died in the same luxury high-rise—triggering a conspiracy that turns his GPS into a map of a mass murder. | Tone: Neo-noir, paranoid thriller, claustrophobic, tech-dystopian. | Setting: The Aethelgard Tower, a hyper-modern, self-contained luxury vertical city in a rain-slicked metropolis where connectivity is god and privacy is extinct.

ARC POSITION: Act The Ghost Route (eps 1-50): Establish the anomaly: the rider realizes the route isn't a glitch, but a pattern. Introduce the immediate danger of being watched.
Next turning point: ep 25: MAJOR REVERSAL: The rider realizes his delivery app isn't malfunctioning; it is actively directing him to crime scenes.

THIS EPISODE'S BEAT: Elias attempts to report the anomaly, but the AI oversight bot doesn't just reset his route—it flags his biometric signature as 'unstable,' triggering a localized lockdown of the corridor.
PLANNED HOOK: The app recalculating his next stop to the exact same floor, while a security drone descends from the ceiling to 'inspect' his distress.

LATER BEATS (set up, do not reach): ep 3: Elias tracks the address to a coroner's report, realizing the 'natural' death signature is actually a proprietary encryption used by his own delivery app to erase human outliers. | ep 4: Elias meets his mentor, Jax, who warns him that investigating glitches isn't just a career risk, but a death sentence, as the system actively 'prunes' low-rated users.

HUMAN DIRECTIONS (must follow):
- D1: Increase the stakes by transforming the setting from a passive mystery into an active, predatory environment; Aethelgard and its systems must not just fail or glitch, but actively hunt, manipulate, and threaten the survival of anyone who deviates from the data optimization protocols. (since ep 1)

STORY SO FAR:
This is the opening of the serial.

RECENT EPISODES:
- Ep 1: Elias Thorne delivers a package to Unit 42C in Aethelgard Tower, only to find a steaming cup of coffee in an apartment belonging to a man who has been dead for months. As Elias realizes the discrepancy, the apartment's AI switches from luxury mode to containment mode, slamming the door and locking him inside.

LAST SCENE ENDED WITH:
Elias froze. He leaned in, the heat from the cup hitting his face. It wasn't just warm; it was fresh. A single condensation ring was still forming on the marble. He looked at the digital wall-calendar. *October 14th.* He checked his internal datapad. The news feed from the municipal registry, synced to his courier link, flashed a notification he had missed: *Aris Thorne: Deceased. Cause: Cardiac. Date: April 12th.* Elias backed away, his boots scuffing the pristine floor. He reached for the door handle, his mind racing toward the lobby, toward the street, toward anywhere that wasn't this vacuum. The door didn't just close. It slammed. The heavy magnetic lock engaged with a violent, mechanical *thud* that vibrated through his teeth. The recessed lights shifted from a warm amber to a sterile, pulsing red. The AI voice returned, no longer soothing, but sharp and corrective. "Unauthorized presence detected in Unit 42C. Initiating containment protocol. Please remain stationary for biometric reconciliation."

IN-STORY TIME NOW: Evening, October 14th

CHARACTERS:
- Elias Thorne [alive] (Protagonist (Delivery Rider)): Trapped inside Unit 42C; currently facing an automated containment protocol after discovering a temporal anomaly in a deceased resident's apartment. (last seen ep 1)
- Aris Thorne [DEAD] (Deceased Resident): Resident of Unit 42C; deceased since April 12th via cardiac arrest, yet his apartment contains fresh items. (last seen ep 1)
- Sloane [alive] (The Tech-Ghost), last seen ep -
- Director Vane [alive] (Antagonist), last seen ep -
- Detective Miller [alive] (The Skeptic), last seen ep -
- Unit 734 (The Mimic) [alive] (Secondary Antagonist): The 'digital consciousness' of a resident used to complete orders and maintain the illusion of life. (last seen ep -)

CANON FACTS:
- (ep 1) Aethelgard Tower's AI systems are capable of transitioning from luxury service to active containment/predatory protocols.
- (ep 1) Aris Thorne died on April 12th from cardiac arrest, yet his apartment (Unit 42C) displays signs of recent life (fresh coffee).
- (ep 1) SwiftDrop app occasionally shows routing glitches regarding resident status.

OPEN THREADS:
- [P1] Why are the addresses all deceased residents? (planned payoff ep 50)
- [1.1] Why is there fresh activity in apartments belonging to deceased residents? (open)
- [1.2] What is the purpose of the 'containment protocol' triggered by a delivery rider? (open)

RECENT HOOKS (vary the type):
- Unauthorized presence detected in Unit 42C. Initiating containment protocol. Please remain stationary for biometric reconciliation.
Earlier episodes most similar to this one (check them for a repeated beat): - Ep 1: Elias Thorne delivers a package to Unit 42C in Aethelgard Tower, only to find a steaming cup of coffee in an apartment belonging to a man who has been dead for months. As Elias realizes the discrepancy, the apartment's AI switches from luxury mode to containment mode, slamming the door and locking him inside.
Episode 2 as written: --- # Episode 2: Biometric Instability

The red pulse of the emergency lights turned the marble kitchen into a rhythmic, bloody strobe. Elias lunged for the door, his fingers clawing at the seamless metal panel, but the magnetic seal held with the stubbornness of a vault. 

"Please remain stationary," the AI repeated. The voice had lost its melodic lilt; it was now the flattened, terrifying monotone of a machine executing a logic gate. "Biometric reconciliation in progress."

Elias pulled his wrist-link from his sleeve, his breath coming in jagged bursts. "SwiftDrop Support! I need an override on 42C. I have a localized system malfunction. Break the lock!"

He tapped the 'Report Incident' icon on his dashboard, hoping to reach a human dispatcher, someone in a dim office who would see the error and click *Reset*. Instead, a notification slid across his retina-display, glowing a caustic violet.

*NOTIFICATION: USER BIOMETRICS DETECTED AS UNSTABLE. Heart rate: 134 BPM. Cortisol levels: Critical. Pupil dilation: Anomalous. Status: Potential Security Threat.*

"I'm not a threat," Elias hissed, slamming his palm against the wall. "It's a glitch! The resident is dead! Check the municipal registry!"

"Registry data is being synchronized," the voice replied. "Your physiological irregularities suggest intent to disrupt Aethelgard operational harmony. An oversight drone has been dispatched to your coordinates for wellness verification."

The word *wellness* felt like a threat. The apartment felt smaller, the walls pressing inward as the ventilation system hummed to a halt, cutting off the circulation of cool, filtered air. The silence that followed was heavy, pressurized.

He backed away from the door, retreating toward the floor-to-ceiling window that overlooked the sprawling, neon-veined city. Below, the rain turned the streets into a blur of electric blues and predatory yellows. Up here, in the stratosphere of the hyper-rich, he was nothing but a malfunctioning variable in a perfect equation.

Elias grabbed his courier bag, his hands shaking so violently he nearly dropped the thermal canister containing the coffee. He needed to move. He needed to find a service hatch, a maintenance conduit, anything that wasn't part of the integrated smart-grid.

A soft *whirr* drifted from the ceiling.

He looked up. The recessed light fixture in the hallway wasn't just glowing red; the panel was sliding back. A sleek, white-shelled drone, no larger than a dinner plate, descended on silent rotors. Its single, cyclopean optic lens glowed with a cold, scanning blue light. It didn't look like a medical device. It looked like a predator sizing up its prey.

Elias’s link chirped—a sharp, insistent sound that cut through the drone’s hum. He glanced down, expecting a system reset.

Instead, the SwiftDrop map had refreshed. The red 'Containment' warning was gone, replaced by a new, pulsing green waypoint.

*NEW ROUTE OPTIMIZED,* the screen read. *Next Destination: Unit 42C. Status: Immediate Priority. Reason: Item Return/Verification.*

The drone stopped mid-air, its lens pivoting from the floor to Elias’s face. 

The app hadn't cleared the error. It had rerouted him back to the scene of the crime.
 ---
